claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 3 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex who is 3 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few more questions:

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! And do you live with Alex, or does he live with someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

Are you or your partner currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex already, or has anyone else claimed Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one is currently getting Child Benefit for him. But actually, there is a situation - his other parent and I are both responsible for him, and we can't agree on who should claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that situation. That's an important detail.

When both parents are responsible for a child and cannot agree on who should claim Child Benefit, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will make the decision about who will receive it. Only one person can get Child Benefit for the same child.

Before I provide my final assessment, I have one more question: Is there anything else about Alex's circumstances I should know? For example:
- Is he in hospital or care for extended periods?
- Does he live abroad for any part of the time?
- Any other relevant circumstances?

If none of these apply, please let me know and I can give you my final eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply. He's just living at home with me normally - no hospital stays, no care, nothing like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Eligibility Assessment

Good news! **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ Alex is 3 years old (under 16) - meets the age requirement  
✓ You live in the UK  
✓ Alex lives with you, which means you're responsible for him  
✓ No one is currently receiving Child Benefit for him  
✓ There are no circumstances affecting his eligibility (not in hospital/care, etc.)

**Important point about the disagreement with the other parent:**

The fact that you and Alex's other parent can't agree on who should claim doesn't make you ineligible - it just means that HMRC will decide between you if you both try to claim. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child, but you are both potentially eligible.

If you want to claim, you can go ahead and apply. If the other parent also applies, HMRC will make the decision about who receives it.

Do you have any questions about applying or anything else about Child Benefit?
